Evidence a rating rests on (S7)

Source: R/flode_evidence.R
FlodeEvidence.Rd

A data.table with a fixed set of columns. Each row is one observation (a spot gauging, a point read off an operational rating, a modelled value, a cross-section computation or a structure equation) and keeps a stable identifier, so that a diagnostic, a flag or an exclusion can name the observation it concerns. Because it is a data.table, ordinary subsetting and column access work unchanged.

The columns are:

columnclassmeaning
evidence_idcharacterunique, never missing; the row's identity
site_idcharacterstation identifier, NA if unknown
stage_mnumericstage in metres
discharge_cmsnumericdischarge in cubic metres per second
observation_timeDate or POSIXctwhen it was observed, NA if unknown
source_typecharacterone of evidence_source_types()
source_namecharacterthe file, system or method it came from
source_versioncharacterthe version or extract date of the source
quality_codecharacterthe source's own quality marker, carried uninterpreted
includedlogicalwhether a fit should use it
exclusion_reasoncharacterwhy not, when included is FALSE
weightnumerica prior weight, 1 unless set
notescharacterfree text
source_rowintegerthe row number in the source, for tracing back
metadatalistanything source-specific, one entry per row

Columns beyond these are allowed and kept, after the canonical ones.

Usage

FlodeEvidence(.data = data.table(), conversion_note = character(0))

Arguments

.data

A data.frame or data.table holding every canonical column. To build one from a table that does not, use as_flode_evidence(), which fills the missing columns and says what it assumed.

conversion_note

Character. What was assumed when the table was built from a plainer one; empty when none was.

Value

A FlodeEvidence, which is also a data.table.

See also

as_flode_evidence(), evidence_source_types(), rating_evidence()

Examples

evidence <- as_flode_evidence(data.frame(
  stage_m = c(0.5, 1.1, 1.8), discharge_cms = c(1.2, 5.1, 12.4)
))
evidence
#> <FlodeEvidence> 3 row(s), 3 included, source type(s): gauging
#> Note: Converted from a plain table; filled evidence_id, site_id, observation_time, source_type, source_name, source_version, quality_code, notes, exclusion_reason, included, weight, source_row, metadata. source_type assumed 'gauging', weight assumed 1, included TRUE unless stage or discharge is missing. 
#>    evidence_id stage_m discharge_cms observation_time source_type included
#>         <char>   <num>         <num>           <POSc>      <char>   <lgcl>
#> 1:        G001     0.5           1.2             <NA>     gauging     TRUE
#> 2:        G002     1.1           5.1             <NA>     gauging     TRUE
#> 3:        G003     1.8          12.4             <NA>     gauging     TRUE
evidence$stage_m
#> [1] 0.5 1.1 1.8
nrow(evidence[stage_m > 1])
#> [1] 2
